options.name: Garden kitchen
options.summary: Make the garden room the everyday kitchen and dining space, opening to family living in the side wing.
options.retained: Current Proposed external walls, roofs, principal suite, gym, cinema, wine bar, pool and garage.
main_changes: Main kitchen relocates to the garden room
Existing kitchen becomes prep kitchen and pantry
Bedroom 2 gains a private shower room
Fourth outside parking bay beside the northern bays
options.tagline: A kitchen at the heart of the garden
options.bestFor: Everyday cooking and dining beside the pool, while keeping the current principal suite and leisure spaces.
why: The rear room becomes the main kitchen and dining space, connected to family living in the side wing.
The existing kitchen stays useful as a prep kitchen and pantry, close to the original services.
An extra shower room gives six of the seven bedrooms private bathrooms.
compromises: Shopping travels farther from the garage to the main kitchen.
The current Proposed front wing, basement and roof terrace remain; the external planning case is unchanged.
options.principal: Current front principal suite, with separate study, walk-through dressing and private bathroom.
options.bedroomNote: Six main-floor bedrooms plus one loft guest bedroom; six en suites.
options.construction: Internal refitting, kitchen services and one additional en suite within the current Proposed envelope.
options.planningFocus: Internal alternative only. It inherits the massing, roof-terrace and neighbour-impact issues of the current Proposed scheme.
options.parkingNote: Four outside spaces plus the current double garage. Compact-car tracking; the retained south bay is only about 4.65 m long.

One wide kitchen/dining opening
Ground-floor guest suite replaces the front gym
Side garden living becomes gym
Original family room becomes cinema
Side bedroom becomes family workspace

options.bestFor: A main kitchen connected to the original east living and dining rooms, with a bedroom available on the ground floor.
why: Kitchen, dining and sitting share the east side of the original house.
The former front gym becomes a guest suite with a private shower room and an independent service passage alongside it.
The cinema moves into the original ground-floor family room; the side wing holds the gym and a shared family workspace.
compromises: The cinema is a smaller four-seat room; the gym takes the side garden living room.
The old basement remains as wine-bar and games space, so this is not a reduction in construction scope.
options.principal: Current front principal suite, study, walk-through dressing and bathroom retained.
options.bedroomNote: Five first-floor bedrooms, one ground-floor guest and one loft guest; five en suites.
options.construction: New kitchen, one wide internal opening, ground guest bathroom and room refits; the current outer envelope stays.
options.planningFocus: External form remains the current Proposed design. Moving rooms does not resolve its front-wing, terrace or basement concerns.
options.parkingNote: Four outside spaces plus the current double garage; compact-car tracking and a short retained south bay.

Separate front wine bar
Wider kitchen and side-living connection

why: A single new doorway links the original east bedrooms into a principal bedroom, study and walk-through dressing suite.
The generous current front principal area becomes two guest suites.
The existing kitchen opens more widely to side living; the rear glazed room becomes the gym, beside the pool.

The current Proposed envelope, basement and roof terrace remain, with their existing planning and construction implications.

options.bedroomNote: Six main-floor bedrooms plus one loft guest; six en suites.
options.construction: One principal-suite doorway, a wider kitchen opening, two front guest suites and room refitting.
options.planningFocus: The external proposal is unchanged. Structural design is needed for the new internal openings.
options.parkingNote: Four outside spaces plus the current double garage; compact-car tracking and a short retained south bay.

options.name: Retained front
options.summary: Retain the original front, double garage, fountain and main stair; add rear family living and a subordinate side floor.
options.retained: Original main facade, entrance, main stair, double garage, fountain, main roof form and chimney; most original walls.
main_changes: 3.8 m single-storey rear living and dining addition
Subordinate side floor with two bedrooms, one metre rear projection
Original east rooms form the principal suite
Ground guest suite and one loft guest room with separate workspace
Four outside parking spaces and an 8 × 3.5 m pool
options.tagline: Keep the front, garage and arrival sequence
options.bestFor: The strongest starting point for reducing changes to the original house while keeping the full brief.
why: The original front, entrance, main stair, double garage and fountain stay in place.
A 3.8 m rear addition links to the original kitchen, making about 60 m² of connected kitchen, dining and living space.
Gym, cinema and wine bar reuse original ground-floor rooms. There is no new basement or roof terrace.
compromises: The original garage is only about 4.95 m wide inside: a tight double for compact cars, with door-opening clearance still to resolve.
A side upper floor and rear dormer are still substantial work; the garage foundations and roof junction need engineering.
options.principal: Original east bedrooms form a garden-facing bedroom, study and walk-through dressing; the existing principal bathroom stays.
options.bedroomNote: Five first-floor bedrooms, one ground guest and one loft guest; six en suites. The loft guest room is compact, about 9.6 m² excluding its en suite.
options.construction: Rear family room, two bedrooms over the garage, original-roof loft conversion and targeted internal alterations. Pool and forecourt grading are additional site work.
options.planningFocus: Retaining the front helps preserve the established character. Side spacing, upper-floor bulk, rear depth, dormer scale and neighbour light/privacy still need assessment.
options.parkingNote: Four outside bays plus two compact cars in the retained garage. Reverse G2 into its bay so both right-hand-drive seats face the 0.625 m central aisle; six occupied-bay vehicle routes and 0.50 m pedestrian routes are checked. Actual car-door opening still needs a physical trial.

main_changes: Side principal suite with study, walk-through dressing and bathroom
Low garden gym and cinema wing
Ground guest suite; one loft guest room and workspace
Kitchen and former garage become open-plan family living
Detached double garage; four outside spaces; pool
options.tagline: A garden principal suite and a low leisure wing
options.bestFor: A larger dedicated principal suite and garden leisure rooms without basement excavation.
why: The original front and four larger first-floor bedrooms remain; the new principal suite occupies the side upper floor.
The original kitchen and converted garage provide connected family living and dining.
A low rear wing separates gym and cinema from the main rooms; the garden link adds pool changing and a visitor shower room.
compromises: The side floor projects 3.2 m behind the original house, and the low leisure wing continues farther into the garden.
A detached double garage changes the forecourt. The fountain moves to the rear garden.
options.principal: Study and bathroom at the front, a generous walk-through wardrobe in the middle, and the bedroom facing the garden.
options.bedroomNote: Five first-floor bedrooms, one ground guest and one loft guest; five en suites. The loft guest room is compact, about 9.6 m² excluding its en suite.
options.construction: Garage conversion, side upper floor, low garden link and leisure wing, original-roof loft conversion and detached garage. No basement or roof terrace.
options.planningFocus: The retained main front is a positive starting point, but the side/rear extent, new forecourt garage, trees and neighbour effects need careful testing.
options.parkingNote: Four outside bays plus a detached garage with about 6.97 m clear width and 6.67 m clear depth. Six occupied-bay routes checked with a compact car.

One side bedroom and a shallow rear living addition
Original loft workspace only; no occupied front loft
Cinema and wine bar beneath the new wing
Four outside parking spaces and rear pool
options.tagline: A shorter front wing with leisure rooms below
options.bestFor: Keeping the current proposal's separate front-suite approach while reducing its length and removing its occupied front loft.
why: A shorter front wing holds the double garage, gym and utility below two bedroom suites.
Four original bedrooms and one side bedroom remain, so all seven bedrooms sit on the main first floor.
Cinema and wine bar use the cellar beneath the new wing; the original loft is a workspace only.
compromises: Basement excavation, waterproofing and a new front wing remain significant construction work.
The front building line changes substantially. This is the most difficult planning argument of the three complete redesigns.
options.principal: Front-wing study leads through a walk-through wardrobe to the large bedroom and private bathroom.
options.bedroomNote: Seven first-floor bedrooms; five en suites. Loft workspace only, with low eaves clearly shown.
options.construction: Two-storey front wing with cellar, two-level link to the original entrance/landing, one side bedroom and a 3.2 m rear living addition.
options.planningFocus: The front ridge is below the original roof, but a lower ridge alone does not make the forward projection acceptable. Street character, setback, trees and neighbours are central concerns.
options.parkingNote: Four outside bays plus a new garage with about 6.33 × 6.41 m clear floor space. All six compact-car routes checked with other cars occupied.
